title: 36.1 A 32Gb/s 10.5Tb/s/mm 0.6pJ/b UCIe-Compliant Low-Latency Interface in 3nm Featuring Matched-Delay for Dynamic Clock Gating
problem: Dynamic clock gating in chiplet interconnects introduces instantaneous current surge (Di/Dt) and supply voltage droop when transitioning from gated to ungated modes, causing data sampling misalignment and bit errors.
motivation: 2.5D/3D chiplet integration driven by AI/ML workloads demands standardized UCIe interfaces with high bandwidth density (10.5Tb/s/mm), low power, and low latency while maintaining signal integrity during power transitions.
method: A 32Gb/s, 64-lane UCIe interface uses matched-delay architecture (internal pathways with identical timing characteristics) to maintain synchronized clock and data signals during dynamic power gating. When power switches on or off, voltage droops (temporary dips in supply voltage) normally cause timing delays to shift unpredictably, misaligning clock and data at the sampling point. The matched-delay design ensures both signals experience the same delay shifts, keeping them aligned and preventing bit errors from voltage variations.
key_novelty: Matched-delay architecture that prevents data sampling misalignment caused by voltage droops when power is dynamically switched in chiplet interfaces.
contributions: Matched-delay architecture enabling robust dynamic clock gating without sampling errors
primary_theme: High-density low-power UCIe chiplet interface with matched-delay clock gating
